title: Intimacy Pact
concept: An agreement for one of the most sensitive parts of a relationship: put your partner's experience first, and make sure saying no never costs either of you anything.
whenToUse: When starting something or turning it down feels tense, when things have stalled, after trust has taken a hit, or just to set this up in advance.
steps: Put your partner's experience first — think about them before just yourself.
Agree that saying no never costs either of you anything.
Have a warm way to say no, plus another way to be close instead.
Say out loud what you actually like — spoken or not, timing and all.
Check in again in 30 days — without keeping score along the way.
If contempt or safety is the real issue, deal with that first.

phrases.text: I want to be close — not in that space tonight. Can we hold each other?
Not about you. Can we do something together instead?
Not tonight — I do want to be near you. Is that okay?

working: A warm no, plus holding each other — no punishment. The next time, it goes well. The agreement holds.
notWorking: A no that gets a cold “fine,” or gets punished — or someone starting without thinking about their partner at all. Being vulnerable stops feeling safe.
activity: Write the agreement together (there's a worksheet for this). Both sign it. Put the check-in date on the calendar.
